messages:
olivia: Zenith ops asked for a tight perf/W validation on their new compact SoC (code: ZN-H1). They want: int4 vs int8 kernels, seq256 and seq512, steady-state toks/s, power draw, and a short thermal ramp. Also want microkernel traces to guide their compiler folks. Can eng-runtime + infra run this next Tue? @kevin @matt take point and post a run plan by EOD today.

kevin: I can take lead. Quick checklist: need firmware v1.5.0, power meter calibration file from Zenith, and enabling small-page kernel flags. I'll prepare a kernel probe script and a run matrix. Tentative runs: int4/int8 x {256,512} x concurrency {4,6,8} x patch on/off. Sample power at 1s.

matt: Bench image uploaded: gcr.io/redwood/bench:zenith-zn-h1-v1 and vectors in s3://partners/zenith/zn-h1/2026-05-03. Smoke command: ```bash
./bench_runner --model llama-3b-int4 --seq 512 --concurrency 6 --iters 250 --power /dev/power0 --out telemetry.json
```Preliminary single-board readout: 705 toks/s @ 78W (idle 36W). No kernel tuning yet.

jordan_zenith: Zenith will share thermal enclosure spec and power cal file by EOD. We can also provide a short plug-and-play script to run on your bench to reproduce. Please include a CSV and one-slide summary for our engineering review.

infra-bot: infra-scheduler: rack-E reserved Tue 08:00-12:00 PST and Wed 08:00-12:00 PST for Zenith trials. Telemetry sink configured to s3://partners/zenith/zn-h1/telemetry/ with 14d retention.

kevin: Kernel PR link will be posted in the runbook. Also: recommend collecting per-token latency histograms (0.5ms bins) and thermal snapshots (start/end). If we see latency tails >1s, cap concurrency and notify #eng-runtime.

olivia: Action list:
- kevin: publish run plan + kernel PR validation matrix (owner)
- matt: run patch/no-patch sweeps on 3 boards and upload CSVs (owner)
- infra: confirm rack + telemetry (owner)
- jordan_zenith: send cal file + enclosure spec (partner)

Please cc jordan@zenith when we send the final bundle. Include README with sampling rate, sensor calibration steps, and margin of error. If thermal throttling observed, escalate to #eng-thermal. Thanks :rocket:
